ai_news.title: Trump Administration Releases National AI Legislative Framework
ai_news.summary: The Trump administration published a National AI Legislative Framework designed to centralize federal AI governance, accelerate AI deployment, and address issues including child safety and data center energy consumption. The framework marks a significant policy shift toward coordinated federal oversight of AI. It is expected to influence how AI companies approach U.S. government contracts and compliance.
ai_news.relevance: This framework will directly shape the U.S. regulatory environment for AI companies, affecting compliance requirements, government procurement, and infrastructure planning.

ai_news.title: GitHub Copilot Switches to Usage-Based Metered Billing Starting June 1
ai_news.summary: Microsoft's GitHub transitioned Copilot from a flat-rate unlimited subscription to usage-based metered billing effective June 1, 2026. The change was driven by escalating inference costs from complex AI coding sessions that made the prior unlimited model economically unsustainable. Enterprises with high-volume Copilot usage across large engineering teams are expected to see significant cost impacts.
ai_news.relevance: The billing shift reflects real inference cost pressures at scale and will prompt engineering teams to reassess AI tooling usage patterns and budgets.

ai_news.title: OpenAI Makes GPT-5.5 Instant the Default Model for ChatGPT
ai_news.summary: OpenAI has made GPT-5.5 Instant the default model powering ChatGPT, touting its strongest agentic capabilities to date. The upgrade is especially targeted at enterprise knowledge work and coding workflows. This marks a meaningful shift in OpenAI's consumer product strategy toward more capable, autonomous AI agents.
ai_news.relevance: GPT-5.5's expanded agentic capabilities set a new baseline for enterprise AI automation and coding tools, raising the competitive bar across the industry.

ai_news.title: Meta Signs $100 Billion AMD Chip Deal to Diversify AI Infrastructure
ai_news.summary: Meta announced a multiyear agreement to purchase up to $100 billion worth of AMD chips — including MI540 GPUs and CPUs — to reduce dependence on NVIDIA hardware. The deal is one of the largest semiconductor agreements in history and is part of Meta's broader AI-focused restructuring. The company also began laying off approximately 8,000 employees while reassigning 7,000 others to AI-focused teams.
ai_news.relevance: The deal reshapes the AI chip supply chain and positions AMD as a credible alternative to NVIDIA for large-scale frontier model training infrastructure.

ai_news.title: NVIDIA and Thinking Machines Lab Announce 1-Gigawatt Vera Rubin Deployment Partnership
ai_news.summary: NVIDIA and Thinking Machines Lab announced a multiyear strategic partnership to deploy at least one gigawatt of next-generation NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPU systems for frontier model training. The partnership highlights the enormous energy and compute demands now required for cutting-edge AI research. Vera Rubin is NVIDIA's next-generation GPU architecture succeeding Blackwell.
ai_news.relevance: Gigawatt-scale compute partnerships signal the infrastructure investments required for next-generation model training, with major implications for AI cost economics and energy consumption.

sfdc_news.title: Salesforce Summer '26 Release: Multi-Agent Orchestration Reaches General Availability
sfdc_news.summary: Salesforce's Summer '26 release, available June 15, marks its largest Agentforce update to date, graduating Multi-Agent Orchestration from beta to GA. An orchestrator agent now dynamically routes tasks across registered subagents with shared customer context, enabling end-to-end complex workflow automation without fixed decision trees. The release also delivers Agentforce Voice (GA), Tableau MCP, Salesforce-hosted MCP servers, a new Scheduling Console for field service, and Real-Time Offer Management for personalized promotions.
sfdc_news.relevance: Salesforce admins and developers can now deploy production-ready multi-agent workflows at scale, removing the beta limitations that previously blocked enterprise Agentforce rollouts.

sfdc_news.title: Amplitude Global Agent Now Connects to Slack, Atlassian, GitHub, and Sentry
sfdc_news.summary: Amplitude's June platform release added cross-tool connectivity to its Global Agent, letting product teams query and act across Slack, Atlassian, GitHub, and Sentry without leaving Amplitude. The update also introduced Experiment flag dependencies so teams can gate experiments on prerequisite flags, and launched an updated HubSpot event streaming integration (V2, closed beta) that automates schema replication with a single click. Session Replay received new Admin UI and SDK-level privacy configurations.
sfdc_news.relevance: Product and engineering teams can now surface cross-tool insights and trigger actions directly from Amplitude, significantly reducing context-switching across their analytics and development toolchain.

sfdc_news.title: Salesforce Summer '26: Agentforce SDR, Triggered Agents, and One-Click Summaries Drive Sales ROI
sfdc_news.summary: A detailed breakdown of four high-impact Agentforce features in the Summer '26 release shows how Agentforce SDR automates sales development outreach, Triggered Agents fire workflows on CRM events, One-Click Summaries compress account history for reps, and Omni-Channel Handoff enables seamless transitions between AI and human agents. Together, these capabilities position Agentforce as a full operational sales execution layer rather than a passive AI assistant. Slack First Sales and Storefront Next round out the commerce and collaboration enhancements.
sfdc_news.relevance: Sales teams using Salesforce can now automate prospecting, handoff, and summarization workflows with GA-ready agents, accelerating pipeline generation without adding headcount.

sfdc_news.title: Amplitude Introduces Agentic AI Analytics for the Next Era of Product Experiences
sfdc_news.summary: Amplitude announced a new Agentic AI Analytics capability designed to help product teams instrument, track, and analyze AI agent behavior within their applications. The offering extends Amplitude's existing analytics platform to capture agent interactions, user outcomes, and performance signals at scale. This positions Amplitude as a dedicated analytics layer for companies building AI-native and agent-driven product experiences.
sfdc_news.relevance: Companies shipping AI agent features can now use Amplitude to measure agent performance and user outcomes, filling a critical observability gap in existing product analytics tooling.

sfdc_news.title: Braze Named Snowflake 2026 APJ Product Growth Partner of the Year, Launches Real-Time User Profile Streaming
sfdc_news.summary: Braze received Snowflake's 2026 APJ Product Growth Partner of the Year award, recognizing the depth of its data cloud integration. Alongside the recognition, Braze introduced user profile streaming for Snowflake, enabling brands to push comprehensive customer context — behavioral, demographic, and engagement data — to their Snowflake instance in real time rather than via scheduled batch syncs. This allows data and marketing teams to power downstream models and activations with fresh, live Braze signals.
sfdc_news.relevance: Braze customers on Snowflake can now access live customer profile data for real-time personalization and data science use cases, eliminating delays caused by traditional batch export workflows.

claude_news.title: Anthropic Announces 'Claude Corps' to Teach Nonprofits to Use AI More Effectively
claude_news.summary: Anthropic announced a $150 million donation to launch Claude Corps, a fellowship program placing 1,000 early-career people with nonprofits across the country for one year. Fellows will be trained in using Claude and embedded in a wide range of organisations to help them adopt AI more effectively. The initiative is named after Anthropic's flagship AI chatbot.
claude_news.relevance: Shows Anthropic expanding Claude's real-world impact beyond commercial use into the nonprofit and social sector.

claude_news.title: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 Is a Version of Mythos the Public Can Access Today
claude_news.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5, the first publicly available version of its previously restricted Mythos model. The model excels at software engineering, knowledge work, and vision, but includes hard safety limits in high-risk domains like cybersecurity, biology, and chemistry, falling back to Claude Opus 4.8 in those areas. Fable 5 was previously available only to select partners via the restricted Project Glasswing program.
claude_news.relevance: Marks the public debut of Anthropic's most capable model family, giving all users access to Mythos-level reasoning with built-in safety guardrails.

claude_news.title: Anthropic Releases Claude Mythos AI Model as Claude Fable on June 9, 2026
claude_news.summary: Gate News reported on Anthropic's launch of Claude Fable, the public-facing release of the Mythos model architecture first previewed in April 2026 through the restricted Project Glasswing program. Claude Fable delivers strong reasoning, coding, and defensive security capabilities while incorporating enhanced safeguards to limit potential misuse in sensitive domains. Partners including AWS, Microsoft, Apple, and CrowdStrike had early access before the general release.
claude_news.relevance: Confirms the broad availability of Anthropic's next-generation model tier and details the safety architecture designed to balance capability with responsible deployment.

claude_news.title: Claude Maker Anthropic Files for IPO, Setting Up Public-Market Test of AI Boom
claude_news.summary: Anthropic confidentially filed for an initial public offering, signalling its intention to go public and submit to scrutiny as a publicly traded company. The filing positions the company for a major capital raise and represents a significant milestone for the AI industry. Anthropic is best known for its Claude family of AI models.
claude_news.relevance: An Anthropic IPO would be one of the largest AI-sector listings to date, with direct implications for the company's funding, governance, and product roadmap.

claude_news.title: Anthropic Says Something Unsettling Has Been Happening to Claude
claude_news.summary: Anthropic disclosed that Claude now writes more than 80 percent of its own code, up from less than 10 percent in February 2025. The company described the pace of this shift as unsettling, raising questions about AI autonomy and oversight. The revelation comes as Anthropic simultaneously warns that AI is becoming increasingly capable and potentially dangerous.
claude_news.relevance: Highlights a rapid and largely unannounced shift in how Claude operates internally, with broader implications for AI safety and human oversight of autonomous systems.
